claims.statement: The per-stack dev-credential contract is two files per stack for the four named stacks (auth, mcm, audit, observability): a committed `infrastructure-as-code/docker/stacks/<stack>.env.example` placeholder template and a gitignored `<stack>.env` holding the generated real values that Compose reads. The template uses `NAME=<generate:KIND>` for a freshly minted value and `NAME=literal` for a deterministic fixture.

The generated `<stack>.env` reaches Compose through two distinct paths: the stack aggregator's long-syntax `include:` with an explicit `env_file:` pin on the specific included component files that need it (auth pins keycloak and vault, mcm pins agent-db and agent-gateway, audit pins opensearch, observability pins observability), and the Nx `up-*`/`down-*` targets' `--env-file` argument for the whole compose invocation.

A credential in a tracked compose file is an interpolation reference and never a literal, and the dev stacks plus the component files they include use the fail-fast `${VAR:?…}` form, so a missing or blank value makes `docker compose up`/`config` abort naming the variable and the per-stack env file that should hold it rather than starting a half-configured stack — but the rule is deliberately not universal: the agent gateway keeps `AGENT_GATEWAY_CLIENT_SECRET` as an optional `${…:-}` so it can come up with token exchange skipped and tool calls failing closed, the optional Control Tower consumer values (OpenSearch / LangFuse / Unleash in the prod compose files) are plain `${VAR}` instead, so a missing observability value no-ops that integration rather than aborting the app, and the backup destinations' fixed public halves (`BACKUP_TEST_S3_ACCESS_KEY`, `BACKUP_TEST_WEBDAV_USER`) carry a `:-` default while their password partners stay `${VAR:?…}`.

`scripts/gen-dev-secrets.mjs` mints each `<generate:KIND>` placeholder with the kind's alphabet and shape — b62-32/b62-48 (URL/shell-safe base62), hex-64 (32 bytes as hex), complex-16 (upper+lower+digit+special from a URL/shell-safe set), unleash-admin/unleash-client (token prefixes plus a base62 body), and mongo-keyfile (single-line base64 of the MongoDB replica-set keyfile content) — using `node:crypto` with rejection sampling to avoid modulo bias, and treats an unknown kind as a hard error naming the key rather than writing an empty value.

The generator's idempotent path is a back-fill, not a plain skip: for an existing `<stack>.env` it seeds keys the template has gained and mints in place any `<generate:KIND>` key that is present but empty, while leaving every existing value — including hand-edited ones — byte-for-byte untouched, because the only alternative for delivering one new variable would be `--force`, which rotates every other value and takes the running stacks down.

A template key that is not a `<generate:KIND>` placeholder is never filled by the generator, so a deliberately blank entry stays blank and a file whose only "missing" key is that blank entry still reports up to date — a rule that no live dev-stack template exercises any more, because `REGISTRY_HOST` left both `mcm.env.example` and `observability.env.example` when feature 080 replaced the from-source object-store image with upstream `rustfs/rustfs`; it survives pinned by a synthetic `REGISTRY_HOST=` template in the guard test, and in production the same name is a Komodo Variable carried as the `<registry-host:port>` placeholder in the committed `*.env.prod.example` templates, which is all `scripts/check-topology-scrub.mjs` permits.

Deterministic fixtures are copied verbatim from the template and survive `--force`: the two LangFuse `LANGFUSE_INIT_PROJECT_*` keys are fixed because the agent gateway and a verify test authenticate against those exact values, and the fixed public halves of the backup-destination fixtures (S3 access key, WebDAV username) are fixed so the integration suite can name them without reading the env file.

Password-on-first-init credentials (Postgres, OpenSearch) bake their value into the data volume on first init and ignore later env changes, so rotating the `.env` requires recreating the service with a fresh volume or the container keeps the volume's original password and auth fails; Redis values, Unleash tokens and app secrets have no such persistence and rotate on a plain restart, and RustFS (feature 080) belongs to that second group — it does not bake its access/secret key into the drive, so rotating `LANGFUSE_RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY` or `BACKUP_TEST_S3_SECRET_KEY` is an `.env` change plus recreating the RustFS service and its bucket-init one-shot, which passes the same key pair to `curl`, with no volume touched.

A container started before a re-run does not hold a newly minted value, so the services that consume it must be recreated and `node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs` re-run to project the value into the BFF env files; the generator says so in its output rather than leaving the next 401 to be diagnosed from scratch.

The generator prints key NAMES only and never values, and a guard test enforces this by asserting that no non-trivial value in the written file appears anywhere in the generator's combined stdout/stderr.

`.gitignore` ignores `*.env`/`*.env.*` wholesale and un-ignores the templates with an explicit carve-out scoped to the stacks directory (`!infrastructure-as-code/docker/stacks/*.env.example`), so other deliberately-ignored templates such as `frontend/mcm-app/.env.example` stay ignored; a parallel carve-out tracks `*.env.prod.example` under the docker component directories.

`scripts/check-no-inline-secrets.mjs` fails the build when a tracked compose file holds a literal credential: every secret-shaped key, password-bearing connection URL, and command/healthcheck/entrypoint auth literal must be a pure `${VAR}` / `${VAR:?message}` reference, an inline `${VAR:-default}` also fails because a default re-leaks plaintext, and non-credential keys matching the name pattern (`*_FILE`, `*_USER`, `*ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `*_CLIENT_ID`, `*_AUDIENCE`) are allowlisted. It runs selftest-then-scan in guardrails.yml's `naming` job.

`scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs` projects the realm client secrets from `stacks/auth.env` into the BFF's gitignored env files (`frontend/mcm-app/.env.docker`, `.env.local`, `.env.e2e.local`, the web-api-mcp TMDB file, and `backend/mc-service/.env.local`) so the imported dev realm's client secrets and the BFF's client secrets agree by construction; it verifies the projected credentials against the running realm before writing anything and exits 2 refusing to write when the realm rejects them.
`gen-dev-secrets.mjs` exits 0 on success, 1 on a missing or malformed template or unwritable output, and 2 on bad arguments (an unknown `--stack` value or an unknown flag).

The MongoDB replica-set keyfile is carried as an ordinary env value (`MONGO_MC_KEYFILE`, minted as single-line base64) and materialized at start-up into a `0400` in-container file by `mc-service/mongo-entrypoint.sh`, preserving the no-host-file-secret model.

`scripts/__tests__/gen-dev-secrets.guard.test.mjs` pins the item #552 back-fill contract in an offline, keyless throwaway mini-repo: all four `BACKUP_TEST_*` keys are seeded into an existing mcm.env, no existing value is rotated, the seeded keys are named in the output, an empty placeholder key is minted in place without being duplicated, a blank fixture key is not treated as missing, and no value is printed.

`scripts/__tests__/doc-env-example-citations.guard.test.mjs` fails when live documentation cites a `.env*.example` that is not actually tracked in git (checked via `git ls-files`, not `existsSync`), because a dangling template pointer reads to a fresh clone as a broken repository.

`scripts/check-topology-scrub.mjs` is the tree-wide gate that keeps a real tailnet host out of any committed file, matching `*.ts.net` FQDNs and allowing only sanitized placeholders (those containing `tailnet` or `example`) — which is why a registry host cannot appear in a committed template.

`infrastructure-as-code/docker/stacks/README.md` deliberately lists no env keys: each stack's complete key set and the generation kind of every minted key are carried by that stack's `<stack>.env.example` template, which is the single source for both, so the README can describe the file contract without duplicating a key table that would drift.

One per-stack env file serves several consumers with different scopes: `mcm.env` carries `AGENT_DB_PASSWORD`, which the included `agent-db`/`agent-gateway` component files interpolate in plain local dev, alongside the `MONGO_*` app/root passwords and the replica-set keyfile that only the prod compose files and the prod-mirroring scratch environment consume, because plain local dev runs MongoDB unauthenticated.

`KC_DB_PASSWORD` in `auth.env` is a deliberate single source of truth: both the Postgres service (`POSTGRES_PASSWORD`) and keycloak-service (`KC_DB_PASSWORD`) interpolate that one key, so the two can never disagree, and on an existing dev volume the newly minted value is simply wrong — the template instructs setting the key to the volume's original value or wiping the volume to re-init.

`scripts/__tests__/doc-env-example-citations.guard.test.mjs` resolves `.env*.example` citations with `git ls-files` rather than `existsSync` — because `.gitignore`'s `*.env.*` rule makes an untracked template look present on the author's machine — scans only live docs (`docs/**` minus `docs/proposals/**`, and `**/README.md` minus `specs/` and `openwiki/`), and keeps a `DELIBERATELY_ABSENT` list for prose that is about a missing template, which is itself checked: the test fails if such a cited path starts resolving or if no such citation remains.

Three secret paths are outside the fail-fast `${VAR:?…}` contract and are named as such by the stacks README: the BFF loads `frontend/mcm-app/.env.docker` with `env_file:` and web-api-mcp loads `mcp-servers/web-api-mcp/.env.local` with `env_file:` (service-local files read by the service itself, not per-stack `.env` interpolation), and `AGENT_GATEWAY_CLIENT_SECRET` is an optional `${…:-}` reference that `scripts/check-no-inline-secrets.mjs` allowlists by name so the gate does not flag the default-carrying form it otherwise rejects.

No stack is profile-gated as a whole: `auth` starts `keycloak-service`, `keycloak-store-postgres` and `keycloak-mailpit` with no profile (Vault needs `vault`), `mcm` starts its test infra with no profile (`mc-service-store-mongo` + rs-init, `mcm-bff-cache-redis`, `mcm-bff-store-mongo`) while mc-service, the BFF and the agent layer need profiles — the agent layer's Metro-dev gateway `movie-assistant-gateway-metro` being a separate service under its own `agents-metro` profile — and `audit` and `observability` start nothing without their own profile. The profile assignments live in the component compose files, not in the stack aggregators — which matters to the env layer because a profile is not isolation from interpolation, so a fail-fast reference in a profile-gated service still resolves (and can still abort) at parse time.

The stacks README's own generation-kind list is incomplete: it names `b62-32`, `b62-48`, `hex-64`, `complex-16`, `unleash-admin` and `unleash-client`, but omits `mongo-keyfile`, which `mcm.env.example` uses for `MONGO_MC_KEYFILE` and which `gen-dev-secrets.mjs` implements as base64 of 756 random bytes on a single line.

`scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs` names unconditionally, in its success output, the one env file it deliberately never writes — `agents/movie-assistant/.env.local`, which carries the operator's own Anthropic credential and which the generator must not become a fourth home for — so an absent file is distinguishable from an unconsidered one; `.gitignore` accordingly un-ignores that file's template by exact name (`!agents/movie-assistant/.env.local.example`), because with no generator producing the real file the template is the only route a fresh clone has to its keys.

Feature 073's backup destinations are a separate compose file, `infrastructure-as-code/docker/backups/compose.yaml`, brought up explicitly with `--env-file infrastructure-as-code/docker/stacks/mcm.env` rather than as a profile inside the mcm stack, because Compose interpolates every service in an included file at parse time whatever profiles are selected — so a required `${VAR:?}` in a profile-gated service once aborted `up` for the entire stack, including CI's app-e2e bring-up, which wants none of those services. A separate file is real isolation; a profile is not.

`scripts/check-no-inline-secrets.mjs` scans exactly three glob groups — every `infrastructure-as-code/docker/**/compose*.yaml` component file, every `infrastructure-as-code/docker/stacks/*.compose.yaml` stack aggregator, and the retired root `compose.yaml` — so a compose file placed outside those globs is not gated at all.

`scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs` warns, naming the keys and the back-fill command (`node scripts/gen-dev-secrets.mjs --stack=mcm` plus recreating the `backups` profile containers), when the `BACKUP_TEST_*` credentials are absent or empty in `stacks/mcm.env`: it would otherwise project nothing, and the backup-destination integration suites would skip — which reads as a pass rather than as a failure.
